title: Ireland Third Level Graduate Programme: Stamp 1G to Longer-Term Work Permission Explained

runs.t: Ireland’s Third Level Graduate Programme allows eligible non-EEA graduates to remain in Ireland after completing a recognised Irish qualification to seek graduate-level employment and apply for an employment permit or research hosting agreement. The permission is generally Stamp 1G. It is a temporary graduate permission—not permanent residence and not an automatic route to Stamp 4.

Eligible NFQ Level 8 graduates can generally receive up to 12 months under the programme. Eligible NFQ Level 9 or higher graduates can receive 12 months initially and may receive a further 12 months if they meet the renewal conditions. Graduates must apply within six months of being notified that they have achieved the award and must meet the programme’s other conditions.

sections.title: Who can use the Third Level Graduate Programme?

runs.t: The programme is for legally resident non-EEA graduates who hold a qualifying award from a recognised Irish awarding body. Applicants generally need to hold current Stamp 2 student permission and an up-to-date immigration registration card. They must apply within six months of being notified by the awarding body that they have achieved the award.

The award must be at the relevant level on the Irish National Framework of Qualifications (NFQ). The institution and award must be recognised under the programme rules. Students should confirm eligibility with their institution and the current ISD policy before relying on a post-study stay-back period.

sections.title: What can a graduate do on Stamp 1G?

runs.t: Stamp 1G allows eligible graduates to seek graduate-level employment and work full time in accordance with employment law. It does not permit the holder to operate a business or be self-employed. The permission is designed to give graduates time to find a role that may support an employment permit application.

The graduate should use this period actively: apply for suitable jobs, attend interviews, register with graduate recruitment agencies, build professional networks and keep evidence of job-search activity—particularly if seeking the second year available to eligible Level 9+ graduates.

sections.title: Stamp 1G to employment permit: the practical transition

runs.t: Complete the recognised Irish qualification and obtain formal notification of the award.
Check eligibility and apply for the Third Level Graduate Programme within the six-month application window.
Register the graduate permission and check the expiry date and conditions on the immigration record.
Search for graduate-level roles that match the qualification, skills and experience.
Check whether the role is eligible for a Critical Skills Employment Permit (CSEP) or General Employment Permit (GEP).
Ensure the employer, salary, occupation, job duration and other permit conditions are satisfied.
Submit the employment permit application with sufficient lead time before the intended employment start date.
After approval, follow the relevant registration and immigration permission process. Do not continue relying on Stamp 1G after it expires.

Not directly. Stamp 1G is a graduate permission. A graduate may later qualify for an employment permit and, after meeting the applicable residence and employment conditions, may become eligible for a different immigration permission. The conditions depend on the permit type, time spent working, reckonable residence and the rules in force.

CSEP holders may be eligible to apply for Stamp 4 after the required period of employment under the permit rules, subject to the current conditions. A General Employment Permit holder may have a different qualifying timeline. Stamp 4 eligibility should be assessed against the current ISD policy; it is not guaranteed by completing a course or holding Stamp 1G.

faq.q: How long can I stay in Ireland after a master’s degree?

runs.t: Eligible NFQ Level 9 graduates may receive 12 months initially under the Third Level Graduate Programme and may receive a further 12 months if they satisfy the renewal conditions.

faq.q: Can I work full time on Stamp 1G?

runs.t: Yes. Stamp 1G graduate permission allows full-time employment in accordance with employment law, but it does not permit self-employment or operating a business.

faq.q: When must I apply for Stamp 1G?

faq.q: Can I start a business on Stamp 1G?

runs.t: No. The Stamp 1G graduate conditions do not permit the holder to operate a business or be self-employed.
